speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have right groin pain and your leg looks like it is turned out. Can you describe the mechanism of the accident more specifically, and are you able to move your right foot or ankle?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned pain in both knees as well, which is concerning given the rear-end mechanism. Is the right knee swollen or unstable, and does moving the right hip or knee significantly worsen the groin pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positioning of your leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is a classic sign of a posterior hip dislocation. I need to check your neurological and vascular status immediately; do you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your right leg or foot?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.
